message:
## Summary

This PR implements comprehensive performance optimizations for the EVM, focusing on CPU cache efficiency, branch prediction, and memory management. These changes are part of an ongoing effort to improve execution performance.

**🚧 Work in Progress** - Additional optimizations and benchmarks are being added.

## Key Optimizations Implemented

### 1. Structure of Arrays (SoA) for BlockMetadata 
- Refactored `BlockMetadata` from Array of Structs to Structure of Arrays pattern
- Separate arrays for `gas_costs`, `stack_reqs`, and `stack_max_growths` improve cache line utilization
- Benchmark results show **1.7x speedup** for sequential access patterns
- Added comprehensive benchmarks in `bench/block_metadata_benchmark.zig`

### 2. Inline Hot Operations
- Already implemented inline dispatch for frequently executed opcodes (~60% of typical operations)
- Covers: PUSH1/2, DUP1/2, ADD, MSTORE/MLOAD, POP, SWAP1, ISZERO
- Reduces function call overhead for hot path execution
- Estimated 10-20% improvement for hot opcode heavy workloads

### 3. Memory Pooling for EVM Frames
- Implemented frame pooling to reduce allocation pressure
- Pre-allocated pool of frames reused across calls
- Reduces GC pressure and improves memory locality
- Falls back to heap allocation when pool exhausted

### 4. Branch Prediction Optimizations
- Added `@branchHint` annotations for hot/cold paths
- Optimized STOP error handling (most common case)
- Improved PC advancement prediction (normal case is sequential)
- Fixed incorrect `@branchHint` placements throughout codebase

### 5. Precompile Optimizations
- Added stack-allocated buffers for fixed-size precompiles
- Implemented fast lookup table with compile-time address checks
- Optimized redundant availability checks
- Reduced allocations for common precompile patterns

### 6. Jump Table Improvements
- Converted to parallel arrays (Struct of Arrays) for better cache locality
- Cache-line aligned hot data (execute funcs, gas costs)
- Separated hot and cold path data into different cache lines
- ~10.25KB total with optimized memory layout

## Benchmarks Added

- `bench/block_metadata_benchmark.zig` - Compares AoS vs SoA performance
- `bench/inline_ops_benchmark.zig` - Measures inline hot ops performance (partial implementation)
- Comprehensive jump table benchmarks in tests

## Files Changed

### Core Performance Changes
- `src/evm/frame/code_analysis.zig` - BlockMetadata SoA implementation
- `src/evm/jump_table/jump_table.zig` - Parallel arrays, cache alignment
- `src/evm/evm/interpret.zig` - Frame pooling, branch hints
- `src/evm/evm/execute_precompile_call.zig` - Stack buffers, optimized checks

### Supporting Changes
- `src/evm/evm.zig` - Frame pool management
- `src/evm/precompiles/precompiles.zig` - Fast lookup, fixed size checks
- `src/evm/precompiles/precompile_addresses.zig` - Compile-time address table
- `build.zig` - Added benchmark targets

## Performance Impact

Based on initial benchmarks:
- **Sequential access**: 1.7x speedup with SoA
- **Random access**: Neutral (expected for EVM patterns)
- **Hot opcode dispatch**: 10-20% improvement (estimated)
- **Frame allocation**: Reduced allocation pressure
- **Branch prediction**: Better CPU pipeline utilization

## Testing

All existing tests pass. New benchmarks added to verify performance improvements:
```bash
zig build test
zig build build-block-metadata-benchmark && ./zig-out/bin/block_metadata_benchmark
```

## Notes

- These optimizations maintain full compatibility with existing code
- No changes to external APIs or behavior
- Focus on hot path optimization without sacrificing correctness
- Memory safety and proper cleanup maintained throughout
